original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: On the PR589 reverse BIT word used by PR #5421, can any subspace of owned helper relations (any dimension, any combination, not only single relations) make more paid jobs free than it costs in lost rank-8 helper targets, after #5421's nine COPY relations? Part 2: the same question on the complex #4610 backward word (the local word of the selected #5383 -> #5398 -> #5413 chain) after #5383's eight relations.
scope_change_reason: PR #5421 removes nine COPY jobs with nine owned helper relations and states that a further BIT gain needs a new relation space; PR #5428 (target 6) proposes systematic relation-space selection. This package answers that question exactly for the fixed source word by a matroid-union certificate instead of a search, rather than constructing a new helper interface.
bottleneck_link: Side result; no new kappa and no new BIT saving. It closes the relation-space extension of #5421 on its BIT word (each extra relation dimension loses >= 0.44 raw moment per local call) and of #5383 on the binding complex word (>= 5.94).
stop_rule: Stop at the exact certificate for the fixed word; do not change the chronology, the word or the helper inventory.
evidence: verify.py replays the reversed PR589 records over GF(2) (2,920 paid jobs, 2,384 with a legal relation row), recovers exactly #5421's nine relations as the only tight subspaces of the source word, and certifies modulo them that 2E' splits into 15 linearly independent sets, i.e. w(V) <= 7.5 dim V < 8^t dim V for every relation subspace V; two live controls fail as required and test_verify.py rejects four mutations. Part 2: complex.py frees all eight centres and eight zero-site climbs with #5383's relations and proves exactly over Q that the 155 remaining pure-cold climb rows are linearly independent with rank mass <= 3, so any further relation loses >= 5.94 per dimension; test_verify.py adds three complex mutations.

open_questions.question: Does a changed chronological order or a different BIT word admit a relation subspace of density above 8^t?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This certificate fixes the PR589 operation order; the density bound is a property of the job rows of this word.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same 8- and 15-part splits on the job rows of any changed BIT word before searching relations on it.
open_questions.blocked_by: No changed BIT word with an admitted invoice is available as a frozen input.

open_questions.question: Can a complex relation set that does not contain #5383's eight relations beat them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Part 2 certifies only extensions of the selected relations; a different basis could free other snapshot options.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate one snapshot option per centre (at most 8 centres) and run the same independence test on each choice.
open_questions.blocked_by: Snapshot options are alternatives for one centre, so they are not single matroid elements; the research/owned-relation-exhaustion centre-exchange cap already limits this family.
